title: KV cache profile orchestration, calibration gating, and chaos experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: build and validate an orchestration-friendly workflow for producing KV cache quantization profiles (INT8 and FP8), gate those profiles with automated accuracy/regression checks, and validate behavior under production-like chaos (traffic spikes, region failover, and fallback to fi64/fp16). Deliverables: 1) a reproducible calibration pipeline that outputs named profiles with provenance metadata; 2) a regression-gating policy used by the rollout service; 3) chaos/e2e experiments that assert safe degradation and automatic rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline can produce a profile artifact (profile id + calibration seed + sample set hash) for a model and KV layout
Automated eval harness runs per-profile and emits: perplexity, token-error-rate, and semantic-similarity regression vs gold baseline
Rollout service blocks profile activation automatically if any metric crosses defined thresholds (perplexity delta > 1.5% OR token-error-rate increase > 1.0% OR semantic similarity drop > 0.8%)
Observed p50 and p95 latency improvements are recorded in the dashboard and match the expected savings within ±10% of experiment claims
Chaos tests: during 2x traffic spike, requests gracefully fall back to pinned FP16 profile within 3s if KV profile causes tail latency violations; no data corruption observed
End-to-end artifacts (confluence, PRs, dashboards) are linked in this ticket
experiment_plan: 1) Calibration dataset: 1000 prompt sequences sampled from production top-50 routes (strip PII). Split 800/200 for calib/holdout.
2) Calibration methods: min-max per-layer, KL-divergence per-channel, and hybrid per-block scaling. Generate INT8 and FP8 variants for each method.
3) Profiling: measure memory (KB per KV), p50/p95 latency, and CPU/GPU utilization for 1k qps and burst 2k qps in a dedicated QA cluster.

4) Accuracy eval: run token-level cross-entropy, token-error-rate (TER), and embedding-based semantic-similarity (cosine on sentence-embedding) on holdout prompts and a small curated critical-prompt set.
5) Regression gating: implement an automated job that compares new profile metrics to baseline and returns pass/fail + detailed diff.
6) Chaos run: on a staging fleet, apply profile to 20% of workers and then simulate region latency spike + request fanout; validate fallback and rollback triggers.
7) Postmortem and thresholds tuning: run two additional calibration dataset seeds and compare drift sensitivity.
metrics: Perplexity_delta_vs_baseline: relative % change compared to fp16 baseline on holdout
Token_Error_Rate (TER): fraction of tokens differing from baseline generation on greedy decode
Semantic_Similarity: mean cosine similarity of sentence embeddings between baseline and quantized outputs
Latency_p50 and p95: measured in ms for generation 512-token window with KV warming
Memory_per_KV_MB: measured KB/entry and total KV state footprint
Cost_per_1M_tokens: estimated infra cost delta from runtime metrics
Rollback_trigger_rate: fraction of experiments that triggered automated rollback during chaos tests
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting. Agreed to prioritize per-block hybrid scaling and to block FP8 rollout behind semantic-similarity checks. Action: Marco to prototype sampler and Aisha to prepare holdout set.
2026-02-18: Prototype pipeline completed. Generated initial INT8 and FP8 profiles using min-max and per-channel KL. Noted that min-max INT8 creates high variance in long-context prompts.

2026-02-25: First eval run (800 calib / 200 holdout). Results show INT8 (min-max) reduces KV memory by ~1.9x and median latency by 11% but increases TER by 1.9% on the critical-prompt set (fail threshold). FP8 (KL per-channel) reduces memory by ~2.4x and latency by 16% with TER +0.4% (pass).
2026-03-02: Implemented regression-gating job and integrated with rollout service. Gate criteria set to: perplexity_delta < 1.5% AND TER < 1.0% AND semantic_similarity_drop < 0.8%.

2026-03-06: Chaos test: staged rollout to 20% of workers with synthetic 2x traffic spike and region-latency injection. INT8-minmax profile caused p95 violations in 12% of cases and triggered automatic fallback within 2.6s — rollback performed. FP8 profiles remained within SLOs.
2026-03-10: Tuned calibration to include per-layer MSE regularizer which reduced INT8 TER regression to 1.1% (borderline). Decided to keep INT8 behind manual review and further sampling.
2026-03-12: Draft of findings prepared and PR opened for pipeline and gating code (see artifact links). Under review by RL and serving leads.
results_summary: INT8 (min-max): memory ~1.9x reduction; latency p50 -11%, p95 -8%; TER increase on critical prompts 1.9% (fails gating). Sensitive to long-context outliers; requires calibrated MSE regularizer or KL-method to be viable.
INT8 (KL per-channel): better stability than min-max; TER ~1.2%; still borderline with gating thresholds; recommended only for controlled traffic tiers with canary ramping and alerting.

FP8 (KL + per-layer scaling): memory ~2.3x reduction; latency p50 -16%, p95 -12%; TER +0.4% and semantic similarity drop 0.3% (passes gating). Strong candidate for broader rollout as default KV quant profile.
Regression gating successfully prevented unsafe rollouts; chaos tests validated fallback path with sub-3s failover latency to FP16 and automatic rollback in >95% of triggered runs.
Calibration provenance (seed + dataset hash) is sufficient to reproduce profiles; recommended we store calibration artifacts in immutable S3 paths and surface profile metadata in model catalog.
follow_up_tasks: Create a lightweight UI in Console to inspect profile provenance and gating diffs (PM + Design ticket) - link to new PM ticket when created
Expand calibration dataset to include long-context tail samples and rerun INT8 MSE-regularized experiments
Add automated nightly drift detection job that monitors semantic similarity and TER against production-sampled baseline
Document rollback SLOs and operator runbook for profile-related incidents
Consider integration of profile scoring into Optimize recommendations (cost vs quality tradeoff)
